page: Microsoft Azure E64as_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Eav6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance features 64 dedicated vCPUs derived from 32 physical cores with multithreading enabled running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The CPU includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

This server runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It does not include local storage, but it is Premium Storage capable, allowing the attachment of external persistent disks. There are no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included with this configuration.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance across multiple domains. In multi-core processing, the instance achieves top-tier status, placing in the top 10% of Geekbench multi-core scores. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, along with Passmark CPU and memory scores, consistently rank in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show strong write performance for large blocks and strong read performance for small cached blocks, though large uncached read operations fall into the average tier.

Given its high memory capacity and strong multi-threaded performance, the E64as_v6 is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads such as large-scale database operations, enterprise applications, and software compilation. It also demonstrates strong capabilities in text processing, static web serving, and small-model LLM inference. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high resource density of 512 GB RAM paired with 64 dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs provides a balanced profile for memory-heavy enterprise deployments without the overhead of local storage or GPU hardware.
